title: The Soil in which the Fruit of the Spirit Grows
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Nature of the Fruit
subpoints: The fruit of the Spirit is singular, not a list of separate behaviors.
Fruit is a byproduct of the tree's health, not directly cultivated.
All nine characteristics manifest simultaneously in the Christian life.

outline.title: Defining Key Terms: Spirit and Flesh
subpoints: Spirit refers to the Holy Spirit of God, not wind or human soul.
Flesh represents the natural, sinful nature in rebellion against God.
The flesh is one of the three great enemies of the Christian.

outline.title: Walking in the Spirit
subpoints: To walk is a metaphor for continual living.
Walking in the Spirit means living by what the Spirit reveals.
This is an objective experience based on God's Word, not subjective signs.

outline.title: The Ministry of the Spirit
subpoints: The Spirit teaches and brings to remembrance Jesus' words.
The Spirit testifies of Christ to elevate Him.
Walking in the Spirit involves testifying to Christ's lordship in all life.

outline.title: Not Under the Law
subpoints: Clarification that 'law' here does not refer to the moral law.
The moral law (love God, love neighbor) is always in effect.
The context refers to the Mosaic law as a system of justification.

summary:
This sermon introduces a twelve-part series on the Fruit of the Spirit, focusing on Galatians 5:16-25. The speaker emphasizes that the fruit of the Spirit is a singular entity manifested in nine characteristics, rather than a checklist of independent behaviors. Just as fruit is a byproduct of a healthy tree, these spiritual qualities are the result of a life cultivated in the Spirit, not behaviors pursued in isolation.

The message defines key terms to clarify Paul's intent. The 'Spirit' is identified as the Holy Spirit, while the 'flesh' represents the innate sinful nature that rebels against God. 'Walking in the Spirit' is explained not as a subjective mystical experience, but as a continual, objective living according to the Spirit's revelation in the Word of God. This involves allowing the Spirit to teach and remind believers of Christ's teachings, thereby testifying to His lordship.

Finally, the sermon addresses the phrase 'not under the law.' It clarifies that this does not mean freedom from the moral law (the command to love God and neighbor), which remains eternally binding. Instead, it refers to freedom from the Mosaic law as a means of justification, highlighting that believers are led by the Spirit rather than bound by legalistic requirements.
